newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end firmer, outperform amid dlr gains.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end firmer, outperform amid dlr gains.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger in thin trade on Thursday, with spreads to U.S. long bonds narrowing, helped by gains in the Canadian dollar and the absence of a bond auction in Canada today, analysts said.

"The market has done really well today, the Canadian dollar had improved overnight," said David Yu, a fixed-income portfolio manager with Perigee Investment Counsel Inc. "The market is relatively thin and there's no sellers."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.65 to C$110.70 to yield 7.093 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 19/32 to yield 6.98 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to 11 basis points from 12 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
"There was better buying today, but I'm not sure where it came from," said one bond dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "It wasn't a heavy flow day."

Canadian bonds outperformed as the dollar rallied overnight to trade past $1.38 (US$0.7246). Analysts said the dollar benefited from a variety of factors, including polls showing that Canada's Liberal government will likely have enough support to form a majority government.
The Canadian market also benefitted from the fact there was no bond auction in Canada on Thursday, while the U.S. market dealt with a five-year note auction.
However, the Bank of Canada did release details of the Government of Canada's real return bond auction on June 4.
The Government of Canada will sell a total of C$500 million of real return bonds with a coupon of 4.25 percent and maturing on December 1, 2026.
The bonds are in addition to C$2.35 billion of the issue now outstanding. Proceeds will be used for general purposes.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.45 to C$103.15 to yield 6.549 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 11/32 to yield 6.75 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds widened to 20 basis points from 18 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.99 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.01 percent.
